description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between an unspecified x-axis variable (ranging from 0 to 4) and the “Missing Step” metric on the y-axis (ranging from approximately 0.845 to 0.860), likely representing performance degradation or error rate as the problem complexity or step count increases. The x-axis is linear, with integer tick marks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. The y-axis is also linear, labeled “Missing Step,” with major grid lines and tick labels at 0.845, 0.848, 0.850, 0.853, 0.855, 0.858, and 0.860. Two lines are plotted: one labeled “CoRe” (orange solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers) and another unlabeled line (blue dashed line with circular markers). Both lines start near 0.860 at x=0 and decline as x increases. The “CoRe” line decreases from approximately 0.860 at x=0 to 0.848 at x=3 and remains flat at 0.848 through x=4. The blue dashed line decreases more steeply, from 0.860 at x=0 to approximately 0.850 at x=2, then to 0.848 at x=3, and finally to 0.845 at x=4. The legend is partially obscured, with the top entry grayed out, leaving only “CoRe” clearly labeled.
